questions.prompt: Keating calls astronomy which of the following?
choices: A Primarily a modern invention of the space age.
D A subfield of cosmetology only.
questions.explain: He frames astronomy as humanity's oldest science and a journey through the cosmos.

questions.prompt: According to Keating, the Greek roots of "astronomy" (astron, nomos) roughly mean:
questions.explain: He derives astronomy from Greek astron and nomos as star-naming or star culture.

questions.prompt: Whom does Keating credit as among the first to think quantitatively about astronomical (and many other) topics, including laws of logic?
questions.explain: He points to Aristotle as an early quantitative thinker who also shaped logic.

questions.prompt: Keating says astronomical information reaches us in basically how many forms?
choices: B Two: radio and X-rays only.
C Three different forms, including electromagnetic radiation (light of all wavelengths).
D Unlimited simultaneous forms with no wait.
questions.explain: He lists waiting for information in basically three forms, starting with EM radiation/light.

questions.prompt: What does Keating say about Eratosthenes' measurement of Earth's circumference compared with the modern value?
choices: A Eratosthenes measured about 46,000 km; the true value is closer to 40,000 km.
B Eratosthenes proved Earth is flat.
C He measured exactly 40,000 km with no error.
D He only measured the Moon's diameter.
questions.explain: Keating notes Eratosthenes' ~46,000 km estimate versus ~40,000 km today.
